question: Can full-lifetime measurements expose the distinction between sample-average and recency-weighted value estimation?
hypothesis: Constant-alpha estimates may adapt differently after hidden switches; stationary and switching controls are required to interpret any difference.

selection.rule: Fixed configurations specified before running; smoke outcomes cannot select a winner or justify efficacy.

implementation: Sample-average matches empirical sample means; constant alpha preserves recency weighting.
The complete lifetime is scored; no learner reset or task identifier is passed at boundaries.
mechanism: Compare stationary and hidden-switch controls. Phase labels appear only in diagnostic logs.
Common potential-reward noise streams are generated independent of chosen actions.
performance: Smoke only. This small nonstationary bandit cannot establish deep-network plasticity, general continual-RL ability, or real-world effectiveness.
